rationale: Grapefruit juice with carbamazepine affected seizure-related tremor onset in experimental animals; drug interaction and induced seizure tremor differ from raw fruit and Parkinson resting tremor.
Apple iPad touchscreen measures childhood dystonia; the fruit is not an exposure.
The Big Apple in a dystonia researcher's profile refers to New York City, not dietary apple; no abstract available.
Apple iPad is a drawing assessment device for movement disorders, not a fruit intervention.

Clinical review reports celery Apium graveolens benefits on motor symptoms, sleep and quality of life; abstract does not identify leaf preparation or a dyskinesia-specific estimate. Original cited celery trial context requires verification.
Canola oil is one ingredient in a 3D-printed emulsion characterized for dysphagia-food texture; no clinical swallowing outcome or oil-grade comparison.
Rapeseed meal protein isolate in texture-modified food is a post-oil-extraction product; nutritional and sensory results do not evaluate consumed canola oil or clinical dysphagia.
An observational toxic-oil-syndrome cohort involved denatured rapeseed oil and neurological/aspiration complications, not edible cold-pressed canola or Parkinson dysphagia treatment.

Single-arm IBS trial gives a multi-herb formulation including cardamom seed; improved overall IBS and altered stool symptoms cannot isolate cardamom or establish a controlled Parkinson constipation effect.
Crude cardamom extract showed both excitatory and inhibitory effects in isolated gut preparations; it did not test oral ground spice for Parkinson constipation.

A 90-day multi-herb supplement including cardamom reported lower constipation alongside microbiome changes; cardamom-specific contribution, culinary preparation and Parkinson response remain unresolved.
Patent claims an oral multi-ingredient constipation formula including cardamom and senna; title and abstract do not establish a controlled patient outcome or cardamom-specific effect.
Patent claims a multi-component coffee with bitter cardamom extract for constipation among other uses; clinical outcomes and botanical identity require original-context verification.

Aerial-part tarragon essential oil caused sedation and rotarod impairment at some anticonvulsant doses in animals; concentrated oil, route and gross motor test differ from fresh herb and Parkinson postural instability.
